title: Taiwan military drill misrepresented as UFO battle video
excerpt: A viral video shared on social media claims to show Taiwanese soldiers engaging in a firefight with a UFO. However, Thai PBS Verify found that the footage actually shows a live-fire military exercise conducted by Taiwan's Matsu Defense Command on Nov 6, 2026, near Fuao Harbour on Nangan Island in Taiwan's Matsu archipelago.
content:
Thai PBS Verify found this disinformation on TikTok

Screenshot from a TikTok post

A video was circulated online claiming to depict an incident in Taiwan involving the sighting of, and combat with, a UFO.

The post included the following description:

And things continue to get more and more interesting

#nightmarefuel

Taiwan UFO: Why the Strange Sighting Has People Curious

The accompanying text suggested growing public interest in an alleged UFO sighting in Taiwan. However, it provided no evidence of a specific incident, witness account, location or explanation, presenting the claim as speculation rather than a verified event.

The description noted that people searching for terms such as “Taiwan UFO”, “UFO in Taiwan”, and “Taiwan UFO sighting” were likely seeking information about an unidentified flying object linked to Taiwan. Yet no details were offered to substantiate such a claim.

The hashtag #nightmarefuel added a sense of mystery and suspense, while wording suggesting events were becoming “more and more interesting” encouraged curiosity. However, the post did not confirm that a UFO had actually been observed, nor did it provide evidence of any unusual aerial object.

The video itself stated that the incident occurred on Nov 6, 2026. At the time of verification, the post had received more than 592,400 views.

Did Taiwanese soldiers really fire at a UFO?

Thai PBS Verify extracted key frames from the video and conducted a reverse-image search using Google Lens. While the original source could not be located immediately, the same footage was found on X, where it had been posted on Nov 6, 2026, and identified as an incident in Taiwan.

The X post was captioned:

Dramatic scene unfolds at a port in Taiwan

A user responding to the post queried Grok AI, which identified the event as a night-time live-fire military drill conducted by troops stationed in the Matsu Islands, located off Taiwan’s coast.

According to the response, the Matsu Defense Command carried out the Yuntai Exercise on Nov 6. The drill included illumination flares that produced orange-coloured smoke in the night sky, as well as red tracer rounds fired from machine guns and 20mm cannons to simulate attacks against aerial and maritime targets.

Further verification using keywords related to the Yuntai Exercise led to a report by Taiwan’s Central News Agency (CNA) published on Nov 6, 2026. The report stated that the Matsu Defense Command conducted evening exercises in Nangan Township, simulating enemy attacks from both sea and air while testing co-ordination under adverse weather conditions.

Screenshot from CNA Taiwan

Using the Traditional Chinese keywords 南竿實彈射擊 (Nangan live-fire exercise) and 南竿夜間火砲射擊 (Nangan night artillery firing), Thai PBS Verify found multiple posts on Threads from Nov 6-7 showing footage of the same military exercise. One clip matched the footage later misrepresented as a UFO-related incident.

Thai PBS Verify also contacted the user who posted the matching video to confirm whether they had filmed it personally, but had not received a response at the time of publication.

Matching footage posted on Nov 6, 2026, described as a military live-fire drill

Multiple users identified the location as Nangan Island in the Matsu archipelago, Taiwan

Verifying the location

Investigators then used Google Maps and Google Earth Street View to identify the filming location.

The footage showed a harbour with several vessels moored nearby. Satellite imagery of Nangan Island suggested the location was Nangan Fuao Harbour (南竿福澳港), a major port in the Matsu Islands.

Researchers identified the likely location as Nangan Fuao Harbour

Street View imagery revealed several matching landmarks, including a Starbucks building and a prominent water tank visible in the background of the video. The angle also appeared consistent with views from the nearby Holiday Hotel.

The Starbucks building, black water tank and other details matched those seen in the video

Photos uploaded to Google Maps by visitors to the Holiday Hotel showed the same surrounding environment visible in the footage

Building evidence confirms the timeline

Thai PBS Verify also examined a cream-coloured building visible in the footage.

Google Earth imagery last updated in 2024 showed that the building was still under construction at that time, with only a project signboard present beside the Starbucks outlet.

Architectural renderings of the planned development matched the building’s shape seen in the disputed clip.

Examination of the cream-coloured building

Map view of the cream-coloured building beside Starbucks

Local map

Additional searches on YouTube uncovered footage of Fuao Harbour uploaded on May 24, 2026. The same cream-coloured building remained under construction and had not yet been completed.

Screenshot from YouTube

Screenshot from YouTube

Researchers later found a Threads post uploaded on Nov 6, 2026, showing a user dancing in front of the same building. Unlike earlier images, the structure had already been completed.

Comparison of the building, roads and surrounding features confirmed that the location matched Fuao Harbour on Nangan Island.

Taken together, the evidence supports the conclusion that the viral clip was filmed during Taiwan’s live-fire military exercise on Nov 6, 2026, rather than during an encounter with a UFO.

Although the Matsu Defense Command conducts similar exercises regularly as part of its quarterly training programme, the progression of the cream-coloured building from construction phase to completion helped establish that the footage specifically dates from 2026 and not from an earlier year.

Comparison between the misleading UFO video and a Threads video filmed at the same location

Comparison with Google Earth imagery confirmed the same location based on road layouts and surrounding features

What are the facts?

The video falsely linked to a UFO sighting in Taiwan actually shows a live-fire military exercise conducted by the Matsu Defense Command on Nov 6, 2026, near Nangan Island in Taiwan’s Matsu archipelago.

The exercise simulated attacks from both air and sea, involving weapons fire and illumination flares that produced bright lights and smoke in the night sky. These visual effects were later misrepresented online as evidence of a UFO encounter.

Location analysis confirmed the footage was filmed around Nangan Fuao Harbour, while additional imagery from different time periods helped verify that the event occurred on Nov 6, 2026.

There is no evidence that the video shows a UFO sighting or a military engagement with an unidentified object.
